images.caption: Figure 1:Temperature versus Weight noise.Temperature scaling controls the entropy of the token distribution but preserves relative token ordering. Adding noise to the model’s weights can completely alter the token distribution, helping the model explore new regions of the solution space.

Figure 2:Overview of noising strategies.Squircles denote model weights (base𝜽\boldsymbol{\theta}or perturbed𝜽^\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}), while squares denote rollouts; each column corresponds to a rollout group for a different prompt. Color intensity denotes the amount of noise added.GRPOgenerates allGGrollouts using a single shared model𝜽\boldsymbol{\theta}, with diversity arising only from sampling.B3POsamples a single perturbation𝜽^\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}per batch and reuses it across all prompts and groups.M3POaccumulates the loss overMMperturbations to stabilize training.C3POpartitions rollouts acrossNNperturbations and applies GRPO to the aggregated set, which now contains rollouts from multiple model samples.

Table 1:A comparison of all methods across common mathematical reasoning benchmarks. Methods with multiple noise samples outperform GRPO on average. Both models benefit most from C3PO’s increased group diversity. The largest gains are on the harder AIME problems. We report the unbiased Pass@1 across 8 samples, and its standard error.
